newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Decision soon on Ukraine oil refinery sale.
newsitem.headline: Decision soon on Ukraine oil refinery sale.

text.p: Potential investors must wait a little longer to find out whether Ukraine will keep or sell 45 percent of the shares in its second-largest oil refinery, a State Property Fund (FDM) official said on Tuesday.
"Nothing has been decided yet," said deputy head Yevhen Hryhorenko at a news conference.
The Fund had said previously that a decision on the Lisichansk refinery was expected this week.
The state privatisation agency has prepared the troubled eastern Ukrainian refinery for sale to a strategic investor, which would be obliged to clear its debts.
Ukraine is due to begin hearings this month to decide whether the refinery is bankrupt.
Fund officials said previously that the refinery owes $69 million for a 1993 loan from Westdeutsche Landesbank AG, but have not revealed the total extent of the refinery's debts.
The Russian-Ukrainian oil joint-venture RUNO has said that it would process six million tonnes of oil yearly and pay off the debts in seven years.
Ukraine's six refineries routinely processed up to 60 million tonnes of crude a year in the Soviet era, but last year refined only 16.8 million tonnes as Russian crude supplies tailed off.
